before:
A correlated subquery refers to the current outer row.
```sql
SELECT a.id FROM authors AS a
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM books AS b WHERE b.author_id = a.id
);
```
after:
A correlated subquery refers to the current outer row. Run this complete example in a fresh database.
```sql
CREATE TABLE authors(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY);
CREATE TABLE books(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,author_id INTEGER);
INSERT INTO authors VALUES(1),(2);
INSERT INTO books VALUES(10,1),(11,1);
SELECT a.id
FROM authors AS a
WHERE EXISTS(
SELECT 1
FROM books AS b
WHERE b.author_id=a.id)
ORDER BY a.id;
SELECT a.id
FROM authors AS a
WHERE NOT EXISTS(
SELECT 1
FROM books AS b
WHERE b.author_id=a.id)
ORDER BY a.id;
```
The first result contains ID 1 once, despite two matching books. The NOT EXISTS result contains ID 2.

before:
This example names a filtered result before summing it.
```sql
WITH positive AS (SELECT amount FROM demo WHERE amount > 0)
SELECT SUM(amount) FROM positive;
```
after:
This complete example names a filtered result before summing it. The first named row set supplies the input values.
```sql
WITH demo(amount) AS(VALUES(-2),(3),(4)),
positive AS(
SELECT amount
FROM demo
WHERE amount>0)
SELECT SUM(amount) AS total
FROM positive;
```
The total is 7: only 3 and 4 contribute.
